title: List Hygiene on Autopilot: Local AI for Bounces, Complaints and Dead Weight
author: Juan Rodriguez
excerpt: A clean list delivers better than a big one. Using local models to classify bounces, triage complaints and score engagement - without shipping your list anywhere.
content:
Every list rots: addresses die, people disengage, some hit the spam-complaint button instead of unsubscribing. Hygiene is the unglamorous work that keeps deliverability high - and local AI makes it continuous instead of quarterly.

Bounces are not all the same

A hard bounce is an unsubscribe; a soft bounce is a maybe; a mailbox-full is a "try later". SMTP replies are messy human text, and classifying them is a perfect small-model task. A local classifier reads every bounce, files it correctly, and your suppression list stays precise - no good addresses killed by a regex, no dead ones kept by mistake.

Complaint triage without the drama

Feedback-loop complaints need fast, correct handling: suppress immediately, but also understand why. A model reading the complaint context can separate "never signed up" (a list problem) from "too many emails" (a cadence problem) - different diseases, different medicine.

Engagement scoring that fits your business

Opens, clicks and recency combine into an engagement score that drives sunset policies: who gets the full cadence, who gets the slower lane, who gets the re-confirmation email. A local model can re-score the whole list nightly for free, because the hardware is already paid for.

The privacy bonus

List hygiene means reading behavioral data at scale - exactly the data you least want in someone else's API. Local classification keeps the entire loop on your infrastructure: the list is analyzed where it lives.
